parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs a hostile parent framework (birth-sex passport regime, entry refusals with fraud-ineligibility exposure, facility bans in many divisions, documented custody harms) with a division that adds its own hostile layer: men's-facility custody and male-guard searches despite a female licence marker, victims of a mob beating charged while no attacker was arrested, surgical-proof-only marker change, no gender-identity hate-crime or discrimination statute, and the country's highest recorded per-capita killing rate of trans women. Recourse is thin: national hate-crime prosecution only, litigation unresolved. This sits in the high-risk band — organised/state-tolerated hostility with failed local remedies — not yet the severe tier, as prosecution of visitors for presentation is not documented.

entry_documents.exposure: National birth-sex passport regime; X markers halted; entry officers instructed to refuse cases with document/sex doubt and to consider permanent fraud ineligibility; travellers report confiscation/stranding; allied governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Ongoing litigation against passport policy; existing X passports valid until expiry; waiver exists but limited.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry screening is the first exposure; a doubt finding can escalate to fraud proceedings and removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: trans visitor jailed in men's facility, searched by male guard despite female licence marker, denied hospital care; national custody policies mandate care removal; immigration-custody forced labour and sexual abuse reported.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented at division or national level; national prison reporting suspended.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A restroom incident or assault can convert into custody with birth-sex placement and harm.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent restricts federally funded single-sex facilities; division bans gender-affirming care for minors; a municipality enacted a severe restroom ordinance; statewide facilities statute not established by the sources.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Two municipalities with gender-identity public-accommodation protections; several divisional classifications have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Restroom use can trigger confrontation, police involvement and custody exposure.

care_services.exposure: Division excludes transition care from insurance and public coverage; minors' care banned since 2024; hospitals subpoenaed nationally; parent proposed blocking youth-care reimbursement.
care_services.protection: Municipal non-discrimination ordinances; national employment ruling as thin recourse.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor or guardian faces care denial; adults face coverage gaps and record-disclosure risk.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parent frames trans people as threats (counterterrorism priority for 'radically pro-transgender' groups, reward memorandum context); division police charged the beaten victims and arrested no attackers; statewide hate-crime statute omits gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime statute exists as a fallback; some municipal protections.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Calling police after an assault may expose the victim to charges and outing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division criminalises puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for minors; parent directive targets teachers facilitating social transition; national subpoenas of youth hospital records; sports exclusion.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor risks investigation, care denial and record exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Mob beating of trans couple (Aug 2026) with concussion and spinal injury; victims charged, no attacker arrested; highest recorded per-capita killing rate of trans women nationally (24.7/100k, undercount floor); 2024 custodial killing documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented at division level; national hate-crime statute only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response is itself hostile — reporting may worsen exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No division gender-identity discrimination law; enforcement recourse mainly national processes; killings undercounted so violence magnitude partly unknowable; statewide restroom rule not established by these sources.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation, civil-rights legal-aid FAQ, municipal protections; two divisions scored best nationally.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved litigation means operative rules shift between travel and arrival.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar tier-1/tier-2 mix: birth-sex facility and custody rules, hostile official framing, no remedy changing the rule. This division adds documented men's-cell placement of a visitor and victims-charged policing, slightly worse than 0.25-D.

0.35-A's worst feature is a polite but unremedied birth-sex facility rule. Here enforcement is actively hostile (arrests, mob attack with impunity, men's custody), placing this jurisdiction below 0.35-A.
0.75-C has a dead-letter statute and ordinary courts granting relief. The inverse holds here: no protective statute, courts/police documented enforcing against victims, so far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a combined regime where the parent imposes universal document and entry exposure (birth-sex passports, doubt-based refusal, fraud findings) and the division adds state-tolerated street violence, birth-sex custody with documented search and denial-of-care harm, criminalised youth care, and no gender-identity hate-crime or discrimination protection. Local police are themselves an exposure — charging victims and ignoring attackers — so the national hate-crime statute is a thin, distant recourse. Municipal protections and pending litigation mitigate only marginally and only in places. Severity is high and partly state-directed; the outcome if outed plausibly includes custody in men's facilities, prosecution, or assault with impunity, placing the division firmly in the high-risk band, near the boundary with severe risk.
